# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)

# Closing a business damages reputation

## Problem statement

Closing a business or community-space card currently costs 1 action and grants no refund, but carries **no reputation consequence** — so a player can remove any card with impunity, including valuable reputation assets. Closing should reflect the loss of the card's ongoing reputation contribution (and reward removing cards that harm the street's standing).

## Users

- **Player (single-player campaign / Endless):** closes cards to free slots; expects the action to have a reputation consequence proportional to what the card contributed.
  - User story: *"As a player, when I close a popular café (high reputation per turn), I lose reputation because the street is worse off without it."*
  - User story: *"As a player, when I close a nuisance (negative reputation per turn, e.g. Pawn Shop), my reputation improves — the street is better off."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Penalty formula:** Closing a non-sold business or community-space card deducts `cardReputationPerTurn × closeReputationMultiplier` from `resourceBank.reputation`, where `cardReputationPerTurn` is the card's effective per-turn reputation contribution on the grid (upgrades/staff buffs included, matching what the income phase credits to that slot) and `closeReputationMultiplier` is a configurable constant with default `20`.
2. **Clamp & boost:** The resulting reputation is floored at 0 (`max(0, rep + Δrep)`), exactly like the Discard mechanic (CG-0MTQ7KUVF009ELQK) — reputation never goes negative. Closing a card with a **negative** reputation-per-turn yields a **boost** (e.g. Pawn Shop −10 → **+200** at multiplier 20); closing a positive card yields a penalty (e.g. Café +20 → **−400**).
3. **Scope:** The penalty applies to **all closeable cards** — businesses **and** community spaces. Legality (`canCloseBusiness`) is unchanged: MarketPhase, occupied non-sold slot, ≥1 action, ownership gate; the action cost (1 action, no coins) is unchanged.
4. **Undo/redo & log:** Undo restores the card, slot, actions **and reputation**; redo re-applies the close and the penalty. The activity-log entry reflects the reputation change via `describeEventEffects`/`classifyEffect` (e.g. `Closed Café from slot 2 (no refund, 1 action, −400 reputation)`).
5. **AI awareness:** The AI's close evaluation factors the reputation cost into its scoring — superseding the current Close AC6 ("no AI changes").
6. **Tests & validation:** Unit tests in `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts` cover: business and community-space cards, the −10 → +200 boost case, clamp at 0 on low-reputation positions, undo/redo reputation restoration, log text, and AI close scoring. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. **Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the core-rules/GDD docs entries for Close.

## Constraints

- No coins change on close; the 1-action cost and the shared `consumeAction` enforcement point (CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) are unchanged.
- Reputation never goes below 0 (discard precedent).
- Deterministic, integer arithmetic; consistent with the `roundInt`/`applyActiveEffectMultiplier` patterns used in the income phase.
- **Balance risk (flag for guardrail validation):** at the default multiplier of 20, most business cards (per-turn reputation range −10 to +160 after the ×4 re-tune) produce penalties of 200–3200 against starting reputations of Easy 500 / Medium 300 / Hard 200 — a single close on Medium/Hard will floor reputation to 0. The multiplier is deliberately a configurable lever so the balance guardrails/tests can tune it (`20 (or something)` per producer).

## Existing state

`closeBusiness` (`src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`) removes the card, pushes it to the discard pile, recalculates neighbours, and writes a log entry — **no reputation change**. `closeBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`) charges exactly one action via `consumeAction` and is fully reversible: the pre-snapshot now includes `discardPile` and the resource bank, so undo already has everything needed to restore reputation. The current Close test suite explicitly asserts "no AI enumeration or tutorial step changes" (AC6), which this work supersedes.

## Desired change

Add a reputation delta computed from the closed card's effective per-turn reputation contribution multiplied by a new configurable `closeReputationMultiplier` (default 20), applied inside `closeBusiness`, floored at 0, included in the log message, restored on undo, and scored by the AI's close evaluation.

**Key Files:**

- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — compute and apply the reputation delta in `closeBusiness` (floor at 0, log via `describeEventEffects`/`classifyEffect`); `canCloseBusiness` unchanged
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — no change expected; verify undo snapshot already captures `resourceBank.reputation` (it does — `snapshotAction` covers the resource bank)
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — add `closeReputationMultiplier: number` (default 20) to the local `GameConfig` interface (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts:52`), the shared default, and the three presets
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — factor the reputation cost into the AI's close-action scoring
- `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts` — new ACs: penalty formula, −10 → +200 boost, clamp at 0, undo/redo reputation restoration, log text, AI scoring
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `README.md`, `src/scenes/README.md` — update Close rules/action table

## Related work

- `MainStreetMarketHand.ts:172` — Discard mechanism: `Math.max(0, reputation − cost)`; the clamp precedent (CG-0MTQ7KUVF009ELQK)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — income phase credits per-slot reputation (`currentReputationPerTurn` + per-business staff buffs); the value the penalty should mirror
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` (AI seat elimination with business closure) — closes owned businesses/community spaces; unaffected but shares the close path
- `docs/main-street/reputation-retune-evidence.md` — per-turn reputation is a tuned balance lever; multiplier belongs with the other economy levers

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (Round 1, Q1): "Is -500 a fixed flat amount, or configurable / tied to business value?" — **Answer (producer, changed):** replace the flat amount with a multiplier on the card's per-turn reputation change — *"multiplying the per/turn reputation change by 20 (or something). This way we would get a reputation boost for getting rid of an unpopular item."* Prior answer: none (flat −500 was only seed intent). Final accepted: `Δrep = −cardReputationPerTurn × closeReputationMultiplier` (default 20, configurable). Research: `src/card-data.csv` per-turn reputation ranges −10 (Pawn Shop) to +160; starting reputation Easy 500 / Medium 300 / Hard 200 (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`); flat −500 would invert difficulty, so the multiplier approach is retained with the calibration risk flagged in Constraints. Source: interactive reply (this round).
- Q (R1, Q2): "Scope of close — applies to all businesses; community spaces?" — **Answer (producer):** *"All"* — all closeable cards, businesses and community spaces. Prior answer: none.
- Q (R1, Q3): "Reputation floor — clamp at 0 consistent with other costs?" — **Answer (producer):** folded into "yes to all four" — clamp at 0 (`max(0, …)`), consistent with `MainStreetMarketHand.ts:172`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (R1, Q4): "Undo/redo — should the penalty be restored?" — **Answer (producer):** yes — undo restores the card, slot and reputation; redo re-applies. Already structurally supported by `snapshotAction`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (R1, Q5): "Activity log message reflect the cost?" — **Answer (producer):** yes — log via `describeEventEffects(0, −Δrep)` / `classifyEffect`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (R1, Q6): "Should the AI factor the cost into close decisions?" — **Answer (producer):** yes — AI close scoring considers the reputation delta (supersedes prior "no AI changes" AC6). Source: interactive reply.
- Q (R1, Q7): "Issue type — feature or bug?" — **Answer (agent Map, inferred):** `feature` — net-new mechanic; the original seed wording describes intended behaviour, not a regression. Source: decision guide (issue-type decision procedure), no conflicting producer input.
- Q (Round 2, summary): consolidated R1 questions with recommendations; producer's single reply answered Q2 "All" and Q3 "yes to all four", and substituted the multiplier design for Q1. Round-2 comment on the work item records the full options.

- **MS-0MV2DORIC001Y9XZ** – [test-failure] income-collection.browser.test.ts > routes per-slot phase data into animateIncomePhases — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG** – Documentation: Main Street card packs (DLC) cross-reference (completed)

# Add state-aware affordability filtering for storyline options

## Summary

Extend `getStorylineOptions` (or add a companion state-aware accessor) that filters out unaffordable options based on `cost` fields. Store the presented/available option list on `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Affordability filter.** `getAffordableOptions(state, event)` returns options where `cost` is affordable (coins and/or reputation gates checked). Options with no cost are always included.
- **Pending choice stores presented list.** `PendingEventChoice` gains an optional `presentedOptions: StorylineOption[]` field populated at choice-draw time.
- **Filtering is stable.** The presented list is computed once at draw and does not change during the pending choice period.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getAffordableOptions()`, update `createPendingStorylineChoice()` to populate `presentedOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `presentedOptions` to `PendingEventChoice`.

## Deliverables

- New/pure function `getAffordableOptions`.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice` populates `presentedOptions`.
- Unit tests for affordability filter.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – When playing with AI player is credit with AI challenges (open)

# Move community space tutorial explanation to the right spot

## Headline

Move the tutorial step "Costs and Reputation" (T13) so it sits immediately before "Move the Library to hand" (T18), where the Library is actually visible in the market row, and strengthen its text to explain why reputation matters (a higher reputation brings more customers and grows income).

## Problem statement

The tutorial step `T13` ("Costs and Reputation", `tutorial.T13.body`) explains that some cards build reputation instead of earning coins, referencing the Library (`cs-library`). It currently sits between `T12` (move the Bookshop to hand) and `T14` (end turn) — several steps before `T18` where the Library is introduced. At that position `ensureTutorialMarketForUpcomingSteps()` never forces the Library into the visible market row (the scan breaks at the next `end-turn`, `T14`), so the step highlights a development row that does not contain the card it is talking about. The explanation belongs right before "Move the Library to hand", both so the referenced card is visible and so the concept lands when it is first used.

## Users

New players following the built-in onboarding tutorial.

- As a new player, I want the "builds reputation" explanation to appear at the moment I see the Library in the market, so the text refers to something I can actually see.
- As a new player, I want to understand why reputation matters, so I feel the Library is worth building even though it does not earn coins.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In `UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`, the `Costs and Reputation` entry (step id `T13`, unchanged i18n keys `tutorial.T13.*`) is repositioned to sit **immediately before** `T18` with no `end-turn` step between them; the step order reads `… T12, T14, T15, T16, T17, T13, T18, …`. All order-asserting tests and docs are updated accordingly.
2. The strengthened `tutorial.T13.body` explains that the referenced card builds reputation rather than earning coins **and** that a higher reputation brings more customers and grows income (mechanics: reputation scales coin income up to the 1.5× cap — `reputationCoinMultiplier`, CG-0MTINZ5GG007BH44). The resolved body is ≤3 sentences and uses only the `{cardName}` placeholder (no hardcoded card names/costs).

## Target outcome
AI seats decide join-fully vs keep-50% via a deterministic, non-RNG heuristic that shares one affordability predicate with the eligibility gate, so headless and Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible and legal.

## Context

- The AI must never attempt join-fully without the coins (risk: AI legality).
- Policy heuristic (proposal): join fully when the event's projected own-board reward (×1.0) exceeds the 150% cost AND the remaining balance stays above a difficulty-visible floor; otherwise keep the free-ride. Exact shape is implementation detail; must be deterministic and difficulty-aware.

# Full-suite verification and competitive balance check (F7)

## Target outcome
The complete project test suite passes with the piggyback mechanic and the competitive Monte Carlo harness shows no unmitigated economy runaway from 100%-reward piggyback participation (risk mitigation).

## Context
- Economy-runaway risk (intake): stacking 100% rewards across organiser events could inflate a seat's economy; the 150% premium is the primary mitigation — measure before/after.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill (/skill:test); failures are triaged via the triage skill into `test-failure` work items.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** Full test suite passes with the new changes (unit + smoke scope, run via the test skill).
- [ ] **AC2** Competitive Monte Carlo run recorded before/after the mechanic (win-rate / score attribution); any drift beyond noise is documented in a comment on the epic with a recommendation. Snapshots are regenerated only when the shift is an intended balance change (see `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` policy).
- [ ] **AC3** New piggyback tests (F1–F5) are present and green.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC7** — - [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

# CSV option encoding and compilation

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Replace the three legacy CSV columns with a single `options` column and compile
it into the generalised `StorylineOption` list carrying candidate successor
sets.

## Scope

Deliver the authoring-to-compilation half of the vertical slice (CSV → compiled
model); runtime resolution lands in F3.

## CSV encoding (decided in planning)

- Column: `options`, replacing `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`.
- Encoding: `label|cardA,cardB;label2|cardC`
  - `;` separates options, `|` separates label from candidates, `,` separates candidate card ids.
  - Blank / absent ⇒ non-choice node (no options).
  - `label|` (empty candidate list) ⇒ terminal option: the chain ends.
- Options are always `apply` (producer Q4=B); `skip` remains available only via
  the programmatic `registerStorylineOptions` seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A storyline choice node can declare an arbitrary number of labelled options authored via CSV in `src/card-data.csv`, each option carrying an ordered candidate list of successor card ids, where an empty list ends the chain.
- The two-way `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` fields are removed from the CSV header and the compiled Accept/Reject semantics are replaced by the arbitrary-outcome model, with no backward compatibility retained.
- `StorylineOption` exposes the option's candidate successor ids; CSV compilation always emits `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and derives `hasChoices` from a non-empty option list.
- The encoding is parsed deterministically with whitespace trimmed, and an encoding that is non-empty but decodes to no valid option is rejected rather than silently ignored.
- One tracer storyline row (e.g. `evt-recession`) is migrated end-to-end and resolves through the new compiled model.
- The CSV column reference documentation in `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` documents the new encoding.

## Notes

- `event.hasChoices` is retained as the derived predicate; a node has choices
  iff its decoded option list is non-empty.

**Key Files:**

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `options` column; legacy columns removed.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — CSV option parsing and compilation.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard.options` / `StorylineOption` types.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — CSV column reference.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — authoring reference.

## Dependencies

- F1 — multi-outcome model contract tests.

# Engine resolution and option tokens

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Make runtime resolution draw the successor uniformly at random from the chosen
option's candidate set and carry the chosen option through transcript/save/undo
as a stable token.

## Scope

Runtime half of the vertical slice: `resolveStorylineOption`, pending-choice
lifecycle, transcript token, save/undo round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When an option is chosen, exactly one successor is drawn uniformly at random from that option's candidate set using the seeded `state.rng()` (one draw per selection, at resolution time), so replaying with the same seed produces the same successor and the option list the player sees is unchanged by the draw.
- Resolution precedence is: `successorResolver` callback (if present) over the random draw over an empty/absent candidate list ending the chain; `effectPolicy` is still honoured for registry-authored options.
- Transcript records the chosen option as a label token; the legacy `'accept'`/`'reject'` tokens are removed and no legacy-save migration is implemented (producer Q5: no saves in the wild).
- `pendingEventChoice` save/undo round-trips an arbitrary option list without loss, preserving the chosen token, and `resolveEventChoice` indexing works over any option count.
- Unit tests in `tests/main-street/MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/MainStreetEventChoiceUndo.test.ts` pass.

## Notes

- The draw must be exactly one `state.rng()` call per selection; any additional
  draw shifts the seeded stream and must be pinned by tests.

**Key Files:**

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution path, effect policy, successor push.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` random draw and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — option label tokens.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — save/undo of the pending choice.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — undo command token handling.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts` — resolution tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetEventChoiceUndo.test.ts` — undo round-trip tests.

## Dependencies

- F2 — CSV option encoding and compilation.

# Validator, author CLI and schema

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Make the authoring tooling model and enforce the new option/successor-set shape
so malformed content fails fast and actionably.

## Scope

Static validator, authoring CLI and JSON schema for the new option model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The authoring CLI (`storyline-author.ts`), static validator (`validate-storylines.ts`) and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` all model the new option/successor-set shape, rejecting dangling targets, empty option lists and malformed option encodings.
- The validator rejects blank labels, duplicate labels within a node, dangling successor card ids and non-empty `options` values that decode to no valid option; errors name the row and column.
- An empty candidate list for an option is accepted as a terminal chain-end, not an error.
- The author CLI can create and round-trip a multi-outcome node (≥ 3 labelled options, each with a candidate set) from the command line.
- Unit tests in `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/storyline-author.test.ts` cover each acceptance and rejection case and pass.

## Notes

- The parent AC wording "rejecting ... empty option lists" is interpreted as a
  non-empty encoding that yields zero valid options; an empty *candidate* list
  is an explicitly supported terminal. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the
  parent Appendix.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — option model validation rules.
- `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — multi-outcome authoring.
- `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` — node options and edges.
- `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts` — validator tests.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-author.test.ts` — author CLI tests.

## Dependencies

- F2 — CSV option encoding and compilation.

# Graph and Mermaid export

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Export the new option model as graph/manifest data and re-render the Mermaid
and SVG storyline diagrams so a node's options and their random candidate edges
are visible.

## Scope

Graph/manifest export plus Mermaid and SVG renderers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `storyline-graph.ts` emits one edge per option to each of that option's candidate successors, with candidate edges distinguishable as random branches of the same option.
- The manifest export records the option/successor-set shape rather than the legacy Accept/Reject chain.
- The Mermaid and SVG renderers re-worked for multi-outcome nodes produce deterministic output (stable across repeated runs) via `npm run storylines:graph` and `npm run storylines:graph:svg`.
- Graph export handles terminal options (empty candidate list) without emitting dangling edges.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` pass.

## Notes

- Rendered SVG artefacts are regenerated in F8; this item owns the renderer and
  graph-model behaviour.

# Migrate five shipped storylines

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Migrate every shipped choice row onto the arbitrary-option model with candidate
successor sets, preserving recognisable branches while accepting the documented
effect-policy change.

## Scope

Content migration of the seven choice rows across the five shipped storylines
(tax, health, economy, labor, restaurant), including content docs that describe
them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All seven shipped choice rows across the five storylines (tax, health, economy, labor, restaurant) are migrated to the `options` model with ordered candidate successor sets, and no `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` data remains.
- Each migrated node resolves deterministically under a fixed seed and the storyline regression harness (`tests/main-street/storyline-regression-harness.test.ts`) passes.
- The behavioural delta versus the old Accept/Reject shape is documented: because CSV options always `apply` (Q4=B), the former Reject branch no longer skips the event effect.
- At least one migrated node exercises a multi-candidate random fan-out (an option with ≥ 2 possible successors) in shipped content.
- Content-facing docs for the migrated storylines describe the new branching.

## Notes

- The migration timeline (date, work-item id, before/after shape) must be
  recorded in the parent work item MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144.

# AI strategy and UI option labels

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Make the AI pick among arbitrary labelled options and make the UI/journal
present the new option list without Accept/Reject special-casing.

## Scope

AI decision strategy, storyline UI option presentation and journal rendering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The AI option picker (`decideEventChoice` / `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`) selects a valid option over arbitrary option lists (≥ 3 options per node) and resolves headlessly without stalling or assuming an accept/reject shape.
- Hard-difficulty static chain evaluation is re-worked to score arbitrary options (including random candidate sets) rather than fixed accept/reject chains.
- `MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` renders the arbitrary labelled option list (no hard-coded Accept/Reject buttons), and `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` displays journal entries keyed by the chosen option label token.
- Tests cover AI pick behaviour on a multi-option node and UI/journal label rendering.
- No weighting, per-candidate conditions or dialog redesign are introduced (recorded as follow-ups, not in scope).

## Notes

- UI/i18n and browser journal tests must run under the existing playwright project.

**Key Files:**

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI option selection over arbitrary lists.
- `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` — option list presentation.
- `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` — journal label rendering.

- `tests/main-street/storyline-journal.test.ts` — journal tests.

# Replay pinning and full-suite gate

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

This is the final verification item: after every feature lands, pin the seeded
replay/Monte-Carlo determinism claims and gate the whole change on the full
project test suite.

## Goal

Verify end-to-end that the new random-draw model is deterministic under a fixed
seed and that the complete project test suite passes.

## Scope

Verification and regression gate; no new production behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests cover compilation, resolution (random draw semantics including a seeded replay pair), validator and CLI authoring, and the storyline regression harness plus the full project test suite pass with the new changes (via the test skill).
- A seeded replay pair test runs both the player path and the AI path for a multi-option node with the same seed and asserts identical successors; a one-draw-per-selection invariant is asserted across the whole suite.
- The full project test suite must pass with the new changes; any failure is triaged into a critical `test-failure` work item before reporting green.
- Monte-Carlo/balance numbers are documented as not numerically comparable with the pre-change build (accepted RNG-stream shift), with the reasoning recorded in the parent work item.

## Notes

- Test execution follows the test skill (`tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` included); no ad-hoc test runners.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/main-street/storyline-regression-harness.test.ts` — seeded harness gate.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts` — replay pair tests.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-player-agency.test.ts` — player-path determinism.
- `./package.json` — full-suite script.

## Dependencies

- F7 — AI strategy and UI option labels.
- F8 — regenerate storyline documentation.
